title: The editing session walk adds captions the way a person does
goal: The one walk that plays a whole edit at Next defaults says the captions 'wrote themselves, nothing was pressed'. Since 2026-09-28 the app writes captions only when asked, so that line tells anyone reading the walk the wrong thing, and the walk never proves the Add Captions command a person actually uses still works inside a full edit.
notes: Scripts/playtest/an-editing-session-walk.json step 3 uses action captionsWriteQuietly (PlaytestHarness.swift ~3944, which calls editor.writeCaptions(quietly:) directly); seed text line 3 and note line ~52 say 'Nothing was pressed: the captions wrote themselves'. The user's ask: captions-only-when-you-ask-for-them (done 2026-09-28). objectives.json now words the focus success the same way (this pass). Find a walk step that presses a menu row or a playtest control by name (lock-safety: a by-name lookup makes the walk refuse on a locked screen; prefer the app's register of panel controls or a menu row read without opening it, see PlaytestLockSafety.swift). Walk-only change: no Sources edit expected unless the Add Captions control needs a playtest name.
acceptance: an-editing-session-walk asks for captions through the app's own Add Captions command (the timeline's + menu, the clip's right-click Audio row, or the menu bar, whichever a first-time user meets first) instead of the harness's quiet step, and waits for them
Its seed and step notes say captions were asked for, and no longer say they wrote themselves
The walk still runs green at Next defaults with its 7 real pictures, within the rotating check's time, and still fails on a blank frame
Anything left rough is written into this task's log, or filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar
